title: Kulārṇava Tantra
summary: The classic exposition of the Kaula path in 17 ullāsas, as a dialogue of Īśvara and the Goddess: the rarity of human birth and the supremacy of knowledge (1); the greatness of Kula and its seven modes of conduct, Kaula the highest (2); the five āmnāyas and the supreme Ūrdhvāmnāya (3); mantras; the Kula substances and their consecration, with repeated warnings against their abuse (5-8); the seven ullāsas; the Kaula yogin (9); special days; Kula conduct (11); the guru, the pādukā and devotion to the guru (12-13); testing of guru and disciple and the kinds of initiation (14); japa and puraścaraṇa (15-16); and the etymologies of Kaula terms (17).

structure.description: 17 ullāsas, c. 2,100 verses in the Malaviya edition

attribution.tradition: Spoken by Īśvara (Śiva) to the Goddess; styled 'the door to nirvāṇa and liberation, great secret, highest of all āgamas' in its colophons

scholarly.text: c. 11th–14th c. (Muktabodha catalogue: Kaula, 'later, post-1100 AD')

editions.name: Kulārṇava Tantra, ed. Tārānātha Vidyāratna with intro. by A. Avalon (Tantrik Texts 5, 1917)

title: Kaulāvalīnirṇaya
summary: Jñānānanda Paramahaṃsa's digest of Kaula practice in 21 ullāsas, on the Kula worship, the conduct of the Kaula and the honouring of women: women are goddesses and life-breath and are never to be struck or reviled (10.87-88); the Kaulas wander 'inwardly Śākta, outwardly Śaiva, Vaiṣṇava in the assembly' (10.94-95).

title: Kularatnoddyota
summary: A Kaula tantra of the Pūrvāmnāya transmitted in Nepalese manuscripts, on the Kula goddess and her worship.
notes: Title recalled from secondary literature on the āmnāyas; content not checked. Verify in Phase C.

title: Yoni Tantra
summary: A short late Kaula tantra of eastern India on the worship of the yoni as the Goddess's seat, the Kaula rite and the kula woman; it praises Kāmākhyā. Summary only (restricted content).

scholarly.text: c. 16th–17th c., Bengal or Koch Bihar (scholarly estimate)

editions.name: J. A. Schoterman, The Yonitantra, critically edited (1980)

notes: Chapter count from memory of Schoterman's edition; not locally available.

title: Mātṛkābheda Tantra
summary: A Śākta tantra in 14 paṭalas in dialogue of Śiva and Caṇḍikā, on the letters (mātṛkā), the Kula worship and its substitutes, and Kaula conduct; it repeats the 'inwardly Śākta, outwardly Śaiva' verse.
notes: Chapter count from memory (Avalon's Tantrik Texts edition); verify.

title: Kubjikāmata Tantra
summary: The root scripture of the Kubjikā cult (the Kulālikāmnāya recension), a dialogue of Bhairava and the Goddess: her descent at Candradvīpa and emergence from the liṅga as the bent Kubjikā, her journey through the sacred seats and the founding of the 'western' transmission (1-2); the Mālinī and mantra system (3-10); the six centres with their deities and yoginīs (11-16); the haṃsa and the fourfold order (17-19); the island-transmission (20-21); knowledge of the three times and yogic departure (23); worship (24); the observance (25).

structure.description: 25 paṭalas, '3,500 verses' by its colophon, which also calls it an extract of a 24,000-verse original issued from the Oḍiyāna seat

tradition.text: An extract from a 24,000-verse original, 'issued from the seat of Oḍiyāna' (final colophon)

editions.name: T. Goudriaan and J. A. Schoterman, The Kubjikāmatatantra: Kulālikāmnāya version (Leiden 1988)

title: Ṣaṭsāhasrasaṃhitā
summary: An expanded Kubjikā scripture of 'six thousand' verses closely parallel to the Kubjikāmata, on the Goddess, her mantras and the Paścimāmnāya.

editions.name: J. A. Schoterman, The Ṣaṭsāhasra Saṃhitā, chapters 1-5 (1982)

notes: Only part edited; rest in Nepalese manuscripts.

title: Manthānabhairava Tantra
summary: A very large Kubjikā tantra (with Kumārikākhaṇḍa and other sections) setting out the Paścimāmnāya's cosmology, mantras, maṇḍalas and yoga.

editions.name: M. S. G. Dyczkowski, Manthānabhairavatantram, Kumārikākhaṇḍaḥ (2009, 14 vols)

notes: Structure not recalled precisely; recorded at work level.

title: Śrīmatottara Tantra
summary: A Kubjikā tantra ('the later Śrīmata') on the worship of Kubjikā and Navātman, known from Nepalese manuscripts.
notes: Recalled from secondary literature; verify.

title: Ciñciṇīmatasārasamuccaya
summary: A Kubjikā compendium from Nepal summarising the Paścimāmnāya's teachings on the Goddess and the transmission.
notes: Recalled from secondary literature (Dyczkowski); verify.

title: Kubjikā Upaniṣad
summary: A late 'Upaniṣad' of the Kubjikā cult in the Atharvaveda corpus, on Kubjikā's mantras and worship.

editions.name: T. Goudriaan and J. A. Schoterman, The Kubjikā Upaniṣad (1994)

title: Paścimārcanapaddhati (Vimalaprabodha)
summary: A Nepalese ritual manual for the worship of Kubjikā in the Paścimāmnāya, ascribed to Vimalaprabodha; one of several Kubjikā paddhatis preserved in Nepal (initiation, the 28 kramas, the pīṭha worship).
notes: Existence confirmed in the local Muktabodha catalogue (kubjikA folder); date and content not checked.

title: Agni Purāṇa
summary: Contributes to U07's entry: chapters 143-144 give the sequence-worship (krama-pūjā) of Kubjikā and her mantra, showing the Kubjikā cult absorbed into a Purāṇic ritual encyclopaedia.

title: Jayadrathayāmala
summary: For the Kālīkula: the great Kashmirian Yāmala of Kālasaṅkarṣiṇī and many other Kālīs, the principal scriptural base of the Kālī cults of the northern transmission (details in U08 and U19).

title: Mahākāla Saṃhitā
summary: A large Kālīkula saṃhitā whose surviving parts include the Guhyakālī section (on the ten-faced Guhyakālī of the Nepalese Uttarāmnāya) and the Kāmakalākhaṇḍa (on Kāmakalākālī); it contains hymns, mantras and rites of Kālī.

editions.name: Mahākālasaṃhitā, ed. Kishor Nath Jha (Allahabad, 1976–79), partial

notes: Sections and editor recalled with low confidence; verify.

title: Kālī Tantra
summary: An eastern Kālī tantra on the worship of Dakṣiṇakālī; its meditation verse on the four-armed Dakṣiṇakālī ('karālavadanāṃ ghorāṃ muktakeśīṃ caturbhujām …') is quoted by Kṛṣṇānanda's Tantrasāra.
notes: Printed in Bengal (19th c.); not in the local corpus. Chapter structure not recalled. Its meditation verse is recorded as quoted: tea:tantrasara-krsnananda:2.syama-dhyana.

title: Kālīvilāsa Tantra
summary: A Kālī tantra in 35 paṭalas in dialogue of Īśāna and the Goddess, on Kālī's worship in the Kali age: in this age japa and worship are to be done in the paśu disposition by all four classes and the vīra and divya dispositions do not exist (4.2-3); it assigns the dispositions to the ages (6.10-16) and describes the Kaulas' concealed conduct (7.12).

editions.name: Kālīvilāsa Tantra, ed. Pārvatī Charaṇa Tarkatīrtha (Tantrik Texts 6, 1917)

title: Nirvāṇa Tantra
summary: A Kālī tantra in 14 paṭalas, a dialogue of Caṇḍikā and Śaṅkara: the formless, attributeless Goddess who takes form for the sake of worship (1.2-5); cosmology of countless universes on the cosmic tortoise (1.6-9); yoga (4); knowledge of the principles (11); the avadhūta stage of life (14).

title: Mahānirvāṇa Tantra
summary: A tantra in 14 ullāsas in dialogue of Sadāśiva and Pārvatī, presenting the worship of Brahman (ch. 3) and of the primordial Kālī (Ādyā Kālikā) as the religion for the Kali age: the name and nature of Kālī (4.31-32); formless and form meditation (5.137-140) and inner worship (5.143-146); the five tattvas with their Kali-age restrictions and substitutes (5-8); the duties of classes and stages of life (only householder and renunciant in the Kali age, 8.8); the bhairavī and tattva circles; saṃskāras; law and punishment (11-12); the symbolism of Kālī's form (13.5-13); and the avadhūtas (14).

attribution.scholarly: Probably composed in Bengal in the late 18th century; some scholars connect it with the circle of Hariharānanda Bhāratī, whose commentary accompanies it; others defend an earlier date

tradition.text: Revealed at the beginning of the Kali age for its people

editions.name: Mahānirvāṇatantra with Hariharānanda Bhāratī's commentary (Muktabodha M00049)
Arthur Avalon, Tantra of the Great Liberation (1913)

title: Toḍala Tantra
summary: A short Kālīkula tantra in 10 paṭalas: the Bhairava consort to be worshipped at the right side of each Mahāvidyā (1.3-19); why Kālī rides a corpse — without Śakti Sadāśiva is a corpse (1.20-25); mantras and yoga; the ten Mahāvidyās as the ten avatāras of Viṣṇu, Kālī being Kṛṣṇa (10.9-11).

editions.name: Gopinath Kaviraj, Tantrasaṅgraha vol. 2 (Varanasi 1970); GRETIL e-text (input O. Hellwig)

title: Kāmākhyā Tantra
summary: A tantra of 9 paṭalas in praise of Kāmākhyā, 'the great vidyā in the form of the yoni' (1.4), who is dharma, artha, kāma and liberation and without whom nothing exists (1.9-13); on Kaula worship and the vīra.

editions.name: Muktabodha Digital Library e-text M00132 (ed. R. M. Caṭṭopādhyāya)

title: Yoginī Tantra
summary: A tantra of Kāmarūpa in two parts on the Goddess Kāmākhyā and the sacred geography of Kāmarūpa, the worship of Kālī and Kaula rites, with legendary material on the region.
notes: Division into two parts from memory; content not checked in detail.

title: Niruttara Tantra
summary: A Kālīkula tantra of the eastern corpus teaching Dakṣiṇakālī's worship and the Kaula disposition, frequently cited by the Bengali digests.
notes: Not in the local corpus; contents recalled only in outline.

title: Kālīkulasarvasva
summary: An eastern Kālīkula tantra cited in the Bengal digests on the worship of Kālī.
notes: Existence recalled; contents not recalled with confidence. Verify in Phase C.

title: Kulacūḍāmaṇi Tantra
summary: A Kaula tantra in 7 paṭalas on the worship of the Kula goddesses and the Kaula rite.

editions.name: Kulacūḍāmaṇi Tantra, ed. Girīśa Chandra Vedāntatīrtha, intro. A. Avalon (Tantrik Texts 4, 1915)

title: Muṇḍamālā Tantra
summary: An eastern tantra that names the ten Mahāvidyās — Kālī, Tārā, Ṣoḍaśī, Bhuvaneśvarī, Bhairavī, Chinnamastā, Dhūmāvatī, Bagalā, Mātaṅgī and Kamalā — as 'siddha-vidyās' needing no preliminary tests (as quoted in Kṛṣṇānanda's Tantrasāra), and treats their worship, rosaries and mantras.

title: Karpūrādistotra (Hymn to Kālī)
summary: A hymn of 22 verses to Dakṣiṇakālī, ascribed to Mahākāla, whose opening verses conceal her mantra ('karpūra…') and which praises her vīra worship in the cremation ground; read with the commentary of Vimalānanda Svāmī.

editions.name: Arthur Avalon, Karpūrādistotram: Hymn to Kālī, with Vimalānanda's commentary (1922)

title: Śaktisaṅgama Tantra
summary: A large late tantra in four books — Kālī, Tārā, Sundarī and Chinnamastā — on the worship of these goddesses, the ācāras (including the Cīna mode), the āmnāyas and the sacred lands; widely used by the eastern digests.

structure.description: four khaṇḍas: Kālī, Tārā, Sundarī, Chinnamastā

editions.name: B. Bhattacharyya (ed.), Śaktisaṅgama Tantra, Gaekwad's Oriental Series (1932–1978)
Muktabodha Digital Library e-text M00119, M00128, M00129

title: Tārā Tantra
summary: A short tantra on Tārā (Ugratārā): it opens by naming Buddha and Vasiṣṭha as the two Kula-Bhairavas perfected by her five-syllable mantra (1.2-4) and speaks of the Mahācīna mode of worship; its edition appends the Buddha–Vasiṣṭha story from the Rudrayāmala.

editions.name: Muktabodha Digital Library e-text M00094 (1940 ed.)

title: Bṛhannīla Tantra
summary: A long tantra on Nīlasarasvatī (Tārā), on her worship, the Cīna mode and Kaula conduct.

title: Rudrayāmala (Uttaratantra)
summary: A late eastern tantra (the extant 'Uttaratantra' is distinct from the old Rudrayāmala cited in Kashmir) on the six centres, kumārī worship, the bhāvas and siddhis; its seventeenth paṭala tells how Vasiṣṭha, failing to win the Goddess by Vedic austerity, was sent to Mahācīna, where the Buddha taught him the Kula way (17.105-140).

title: Gandharva Tantra
summary: A late tantra on the worship of Tripurasundarī and other goddesses used in eastern India, with Kaula elements.
notes: Present in the local catalogue (northeast Indian tantra); content not checked.

title: Phetkāriṇī Tantra
summary: An eastern tantra of the Kālī–Tārā cycle concerned with mantras and the six magical acts.
notes: Present in the local catalogue; content not checked.

title: Viśvasāra Tantra
summary: An eastern tantra on Kālī and the Mahāvidyās, cited by the Bengali digests.
notes: Present in the local catalogue; content not checked.

title: Bhuvaneśvarīrahasya
summary: A manual on the worship of the Mahāvidyā Bhuvaneśvarī.
notes: Attributed in some editions to Pṛthvīdharācārya; attribution not checked.

title: Kālikā Purāṇa
summary: For the Bengal–Assam lineage: the Upapurāṇa of Kāmarūpa, telling Satī's death, Śiva's grief and the scattering of her body into the pīṭhas (feet at Devīkūṭa, thighs at Uḍḍīyāna, yoni at Kāmagiri in Kāmarūpa, breasts at Jālandhara, shoulders and neck at Pūrṇagiri) (ch. 18 in the Vaṅgavāsī ed.); the worship of Kāmākhyā and of Tripurā; and the chapter on offerings (the 'rudhirādhyāya', ch. 67 in that edition), with its substitutes and prohibitions (summary only).

editions.name: Muktabodha Digital Library e-text M00405 (Vaṅgavāsī ed., Calcutta 1909)

notes: Chapter numbering differs between editions (the offering chapter is often cited as ch. 71 in other editions).

title: Bṛhaddharma Purāṇa
summary: A Bengali Upapurāṇa in three khaṇḍas: its Madhyakhaṇḍa tells how Satī, refused leave by Śiva to attend Dakṣa's sacrifice, reveals herself as the root Nature and shows him her ten Mahāvidyā forms in the ten directions (madhya 6); it also treats the Gaṅgā, the ages and dharma.

editions.name: eBhāratī-sampat e-text (continuous chapter numbering: madhya 6 = ch. 36)

title: Mahābhāgavata Purāṇa
summary: For the Kālīkula: the Bengali Śākta Upapurāṇa in which Satī, angered at Śiva's refusal, manifests the ten Mahāvidyās who surround him in the ten directions (ch. 8), the classic account of their origin.
notes: Chapter number (8) recalled, not checked; the text is not in the local corpus.

title: Tantrasāra (Bṛhattantrasāra) of Kṛṣṇānanda Āgamavāgīśa
summary: The great Bengali digest of tantric worship in paricchedas: initiation and its preliminaries (including the checks of a mantra's suitability, which the Mahāvidyās are said not to need — a statement Kṛṣṇānanda reads as praise), then the mantras, meditations and worship of Viṣṇu, Śrīvidyā, the Mahāvidyās and above all Dakṣiṇakālī (Śyāmā), quoting the Kālī Tantra's meditation verse; yoginī-sādhana, homa, mudrās.

tradition.text: Kṛṣṇānanda is remembered as a contemporary of Caitanya at Navadvīpa

editions.name: Muktabodha Digital Library e-text M00013 (Kāśī ed.)

title: Śāktānandataraṅgiṇī
summary: Brahmānanda Giri's digest on Śākta worship: the guru and initiation, the dispositions, the five tattvas and the worship of Kālī and Tārā.

editions.name: Muktabodha Digital Library e-text M00134 (ed. Pañcānana Śāstrī)

title: Tārārahasya
summary: Brahmānanda's manual of the worship of Tārā, with a commentary (vṛtti).

editions.name: Muktabodha Digital Library e-text M00095, M00323

notes: Identity of 'Brahmānanda' of the Tārārahasya with Brahmānanda Giri is the usual view; not checked.

title: Tārābhaktisudhārṇava
summary: Narasiṃha Ṭhakkura's large Mithilā digest on the worship of Tārā, arranged in 'waves' (taraṅgas).

title: Śyāmārahasya
summary: Pūrṇānanda's digest of the worship of Śyāmā (Dakṣiṇakālī), widely used in Bengal.
notes: Not in the local corpus; printed editions exist (Calcutta).

title: Śrītattvacintāmaṇi
summary: Pūrṇānanda's digest of tantric worship in prakāśas; its sixth prakāśa ('yogavivaraṇa') is the Ṣaṭcakranirūpaṇa, the classic Śākta description of the six centres and the rising of kuṇḍalinī.
notes: Sixth prakāśa = src:sat-cakra-nirupana (U28 owns that id).

title: Sarvollāsa Tantra
summary: A compendium ascribed to Sarvānanda (Sarvānandanātha) of Mehar, gathering tantric passages on the worship of all the Mahāvidyās.

title: Prāṇatoṣiṇī
summary: Rāmatoṣaṇa Vidyālaṅkāra's vast Bengali compilation of tantric material in kāṇḍas (sarga, dharma, artha, kāmya, bhakti…), completed in the early 19th century.

editions.name: Muktabodha Digital Library e-text M00060, M00061, M00070-M00073

title: Pīṭhanirṇaya (Mahāpīṭhanirūpaṇa)
summary: A late list of the fifty-one Śākta seats, naming for each the part of Satī's body or ornament that fell there, the Goddess and her guardian Bhairava; ascribed to the Tantracūḍāmaṇi.
notes: Not in the local corpus; attribution to the Tantracūḍāmaṇi and date as usually reported (D. C. Sircar, The Śākta Pīṭhas). Verify.

title: Rāmprasādī songs (Rāmprasād's padāvalī)
summary: The Bengali songs of Rāmprasād Sen to Kālī (Śyāmā-saṅgīt) and to Umā (āgamanī–vijayā): the devotee as the Mother's child who pleads with, reproaches and surrenders to her; the mind addressed as a farmer who lets the field of human life lie fallow; the world as a 'frame of illusion'; Kālī's name as the refuge at death. The songs are transmitted orally and in 19th-century collections, so wording and attribution vary.
notes: Attribution of individual songs to Rāmprasād is often uncertain; later songs in his style ('Rāmprasādī sur') circulate under his name.

title: Kavirañjana Vidyāsundara (Rāmprasād)
summary: Rāmprasād's Bengali narrative poem on the Vidyā–Sundara love story, framed by praise of Kālī.

title: Kālīkīrtana (Rāmprasād)
summary: Rāmprasād's Bengali poem on the childhood and play of Umā/Kālī.

title: Kamalākānta's Śyāmā-saṅgīt
summary: The Bengali songs of Kamalākānta Bhaṭṭācārya to Kālī/Śyāmā and to Umā, in which the Mother's blackness is questioned and affirmed as the colour of the formless, and the devotee's mind is urged to rest in her.

title: Sādhaka-rañjana (Kamalākānta)
summary: Kamalākānta's Bengali verse treatise on Śākta tantric yoga: the six centres, kuṇḍalinī and the inner worship.
notes: Title and subject recalled from literary histories; verify.

title: Caṇḍīmaṅgala (Mukundarām Cakravartī)
summary: The best-known Bengali 'auspicious poem' of the Goddess Caṇḍī, telling of her grace to the hunter Kālaketu and the merchant Dhanapati and his son Śrīmanta; a narrative source for popular Śākta devotion in Bengal.

title: Annadāmaṅgala (Bhāratcandra Rāy)
summary: Bhāratcandra's Bengali poem in praise of Annapūrṇā/Annadā, composed at the court of Rājā Kṛṣṇacandra of Nadia; it includes the Vidyāsundara episode and the story of Satī and the pīṭhas.
